To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new formal model, RAS, for real-time architectural design, and we have developed a method for verifying timing requirements of the RAS model.

we developed a formal method that integrates timing requirements into the design modeling and verification of command and control (or other real-time distributed) systems and we demonstrated the method by applying it to the development of an integrated air defense (IAD) command and control system.
the RAS model provides a formal framework for the design and verification of C2 systems and that our incremental method for verifying RAS models is effective in reducing verification complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a formal foundation that integrates architectural modeling and analysis to support the design of highly reliable real time systems.
the development of a methodology and tools that can help designers to develop C2 systems that can be formally analyzed and verified.
the development of a methodology that integrates formal techniques into a systematic and incremental process of architectural modeling for C2 systems design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RAS approach provides an effective and systematic way to enforce the system requirements and timing constraints in the design and verification of real-time distributed systems, especially for the command and control system.

the RAS model is a suitable formal system for architectural specification, analysis, and design of C2 system and that the incremental method for verifying RAS models is a promising approach for verifying timing requirements of a C2 system.
RAS provides a formal foundation that enables us to integrate existing formal techniques into practical and scale-able methods for C2 system design and verification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided an integrated architectural modeling and analysis method that is based on formal methods for the design of real-time distributed systems, and we have shown that the method is applicable to the design of C3 systems.
RAS provides a framework that supports a formal and incremental design process.
RAS provides a formal foundation that enables us to integrate existing formal techniques into practical engineering methods that can be used in the development of highly dependable systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formal methods can be integrated into the system design process and be made practical and scaleable for the design of real-time distributed systems.
the formal methods for system design, modeling and analysis are not only useful but also essential for high-assurance systems.
the RAS model can be incrementally constructed and incrementally verified.
